items: Evolving is much quicker: eating a berry is a quick nibble with a sparkle, and babies evolve after just 1 berry, young after 3, adults after 8
Berries grow in patches of a few bushes, clusters of red glints you can spot
Party animals run to a berry at the same pace they follow you, a quick hop rather than a slow amble
Party animals take berries on their way: following you, they nip over to one near their path; set a sigil in the middle of a patch and they'll eat their way round it
Placed sigils are easier to see: the grass is trampled flat round them, and their runes glow a little brighter
Trunks stay visible in short, dense woods like the tangly forest: only their top part fades where the crowns are hidden
Berries: every area has bushes with shiny dark-red berries (8–12 per area), glowing softly at night and glinting red through the treetops
Party animals walk over to a berry near them and eat it; it grows again somewhere else in the forest

Feed a party animal enough berries and it evolves (babies after 5, young after 10, adults after 30): it glows and pulses for a bar, then flashes into its next size with a burst of sparkles, and the dancefloor flashes in its colour. Adults become legends: the only way to get a party legend
A red ring round each party animal shows how close it is to evolving (near the witch, and just after it eats). Debug: B feeds the nearest party animal a berry
At the start the speakers round the dancefloor boot up one by one, giving you about a minute before the countdown to the first wave begins
A spell: Q (gamepad B, touch 'spell') casts a speed boost: much faster for a few seconds, with a trail; the ring in the corner shows it recharging
Cycle: C (gamepad right-stick click, touch 'cycle') sends the bottom sigil of your stack to the top, so you choose which creature goes down next
A few creatures (hares, stoats, martens) are quick on their feet; legends are very slow; you're still much faster than any of them
The witch is lit by the lights around her: she turns red by a red soundsystem, warm by a campfire, and catches a coloured rim on the side facing a light, while staying easy to see in the dark

Forecasting: the next two areas to join the party are certain, and a few more are likely. Their rune stones grow rings of magic symbols, a full ring of 12 on the next one, and their beams grow as the countdown runs
A smaller, dimmer cue at the screen's edge points to the area after next
Music: a beat plays, loud and clear near the dancefloor and other playing soundsystems, quiet and muffled deep in the forest, and crackling when a speaker nearby is damaged (?music=off)
The new treehouse: a tall timber tower in a giant tree, its turret above the treetops; you start at the decks in its studio, and step down out of it when you set off

Scenes to find: a farmyard corner, a bus stop, a picnic gone wild, an allotment, festival remnants, a cemetery, a car park, a scrap yard, ruined churches and temples, castle ruins and more, each one at most once per map
Tractors, hay bales, fences, gates, lampposts, road signs and other countryside and street finds turn up in the forest, each one at most once per map
No more 'land to talk' prompt
The dancefloor's old soundsystem is gone; its ring of speakers carries the music
The next-stone arrow now points the right way
The next-stone cue shows the area's rune, and its ring fills as the countdown to the next wave runs
The party's border twinkles and flickers between the colours of the areas on either side
Flying straight up or down the screen, the witch is seen from behind or coming at you
